accuracy.evidence: Checked against the British Beekeepers' Association leaflet 'The honey bee colony', the Bumblebee Conservation Trust, the Natural History Museum's ant pages and von Frisch's dance-language work: one queen who lays the eggs (up to about 2,000 a day at peak, used as the top of the p2 range), female workers, male drones with no sting that collect no food; age polyethism for a summer worker (cleaning cells days 1–2, nursing about 3–11, wax and comb about 12–17, guarding about 18–21, foraging after about day 22, life about 5–6 weeks), which the lab and text state as 'about' because the ages shift with colony needs. Waggle run angle from vertical equals the food's angle from the sun's azimuth and run duration grows with distance. Ant workers are female and lay a trail pheromone that fades without reinforcement. Most of the 20,000-plus bee species are solitary; all ants are eusocial; bumblebee colonies hold a few hundred and last one season.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the ideas teachers and the BBKA education material report: the queen is the boss (Ann, m2, visual card 'The queen gives the orders'), workers are male / drones do the work (Dee, m6, step 1 predict option 'The drones', card 'Drones fetch the food'), a new worker flies out for food first (step 2 predict, wrong-order job feedback naming the start day, challenge tag age), the dance shows distance by something other than waggle length (step 3 predict 'By the colour of the bee', wrong-distance feedback), ants find food by sight or orders (p5 and challenge tags see and boss), and all bees live in hives (Gia, mason and leafcutter bee cards, m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). The related labs are 878 flaginsect (assembling the insect body plan), 547 flagbug and 696 flagmbhab (what a minibeast is and where it lives) and 863 flagmbmove (how minibeasts move). None models a division of labour that changes with age, a waggle dance decoded against the sun's direction on a field map, or a pheromone trail that a scout draws and nestmates then follow; these mechanisms belong to social insects only.

lab_teaches.evidence: Sorting seven job cards into queen, worker and drone boxes shows that the workers' box fills up, so 'workers do almost everything' is discovered before the text confirms it. Dragging the bee along a 38-day line lights up where she works (inside, door, flowers) and the job chips must be tapped in age order, so 'inside first, out last' is found by trying. Each dance is decoded on a map with the hive-to-sun line drawn, and two flowers share a direction but differ in distance, so the learner must use both angle and waggle length. The scout ant's own dragged path becomes the trail the others walk along.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks who does most jobs with 'The queen' as the tempting answer, disproved when four of seven cards land in Worker. Step 2 asks a new worker's first job with 'Flying out for nectar' as the tempting answer, disproved by the lit 'Inside the hive' zone at day 1 and the refusal to accept Fetch food first. Step 3 asks how the dance shows distance with 'By the colour of the bee' and 'It cannot show that' as wrong options; the lab shows two dances pointing the same way that differ only in waggle length and lead to Clover and Heather.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Each wrong option carries a tag with its own message: eggs ('Only the queen lays eggs. Workers fetch food, build, clean and guard; drones are the males'), drone ('A drone is a male bee. He has no sting and does not work'), age ('A new worker starts with cleaning cells…'), up ('Up on the comb stands for the sun…'), len ('The length of the waggle shows the distance…'), boss and see for the ant trail. In the lab, wrong sorts name the job's true owner, wrong dance taps say whether the way or the distance was wrong, and wrong job order names the day each job starts.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 2.9 (limit 6.5) and the adult text grade 9.4 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('A honeybee hive has one queen. She lays all the eggs'), each new word (colony, drone, waggle dance, scent trail) is explained where it first appears, and lab headings are four words or fewer.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. Every kid paragraph carries a fact the lab tests (colony and jobs, the three kinds of bee, the age order of jobs, dance and scent trail plus 'nobody is the boss'); the adult text gives curriculum links, the six tasks and the named mistakes with no repeated template sentences; each item hint points back to a specific lab step.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android) in light and dark themes and at 1200 px desktop: the three job boxes fit with their sorted cards readable at 10 px+, the 38-day line, three zones and five job chips fit without clipping, the dance field shows the comb inset, sun line and three labelled flowers with no overlapping labels after moving Heather's label right and Lime tree's above, and the trail map shows nest, food and the drawn path. Every action also has a 44 px button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completes with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (three or two sort boxes, Younger/Older plus five job buttons, three flower buttons, 'Walk the scout home', '<name> is right'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the card, the bee's day and job, the dance angle and length with every flower's direction, or the scout's progress.
